chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Sulayman ibn Harun al-Ijli, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'I do not think that anyone whose mouth is opened with water from the Euphrates will not love us, the Ahl al-Bayt.' Then he asked me: 'What is the distance between you and the water of the Euphrates?' I informed him, and he said: 'If I were there, I would love to go to it at the two ends of the day.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ: The two ends of the day (morning and evening)
key_terms.يُحَنَّكُ: The act of opening a newborn's mouth with a sweet substance (like dates) after birth

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Euphrates River in relation to the Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical act of drinking or being sprinkled with Euphrates water to spiritual affinity with the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the river's status as a blessed source of purity in Shia tradition. His personal desire to visit it 'twice a day' underscores the Euphrates' significance not merely as a geographical landmark but as a sacred locus for devotion and connection to the Imams.
